_notes: One entry per measure: unit, period type and an ordered priority list of XBRL concepts. The first concept with a value for a fiscal year wins, year by year. An object {"sum": [...]} is an explicit derived value (all parts must exist). Reviewed against the 5 fixtures; see docs/coverage_report.md.

concepts.note: bank net revenue: net interest income plus noninterest income (ADR-061)

revenue._notes: component_guard 0.5 (ADR-061): a candidate worth less than half of the largest candidate for the same year is a component (General Mills' `Revenues` was $2.0B against $19B total in 2019-2024, Hershey's $1.5B, Camden's fee line $0.01B), so it is skipped. Companies switch tags over time (GOOGL, TSLA, DUK). Banks tag total net revenue as Revenues (JPM). SalesRevenueGoodsNet is last so it only fills years nothing else covers (KO 2007-2017). The two lease-income concepts (ADR-064) are the last resort for REITs that tag no `Revenues` (Camden Property Trust: `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax` is a $0.01B non-lease component and rental income is $1.57B); the guard above skips the component, and lease income is within a few percent of total revenue for the REITs that report both.

net_income._notes: NetIncomeLoss is attributable to the parent; ProfitLoss includes noncontrolling interests, so it is only a fallback.

eps_diluted._notes: TSLA used BasicAndDiluted in its loss-making years.

current_assets._notes: Banks do not report a classified balance sheet, so JPM is a gap.

long_term_debt._notes: Non-current portion first (Graham's test is on long-term debt). LongTermDebt includes the current portion, so it is a last resort.

stockholders_equity._notes: Parent shareholders' equity first, to match parent net income in ROE.

concepts.note: derived: revenues minus costs and expenses, from the same filing and period, and proven equal to the company's reported operating income in at least 2 overlapping years, and used only from the first proven year onward (ADR-064)

operating_income._notes: Banks do not report operating income (JPM is a gap). The derived difference (ADR-064) fills the years after a company stopped tagging OperatingIncomeLoss (Boston Properties and Public Storage from FY2018), and only when A - B equals the reported value within 1% in every overlapping year; years before the first proven one are not filled (Ford's 2007-2016 differ in presentation). Without that proof it is not used: of the 14 non-financial companies that have no OperatingIncomeLoss at all but tag both concepts, 7 have A - B equal to pre-tax income in every year (Chevron, Bristol-Myers Squibb, HCA, Textron, Ventas, Welltower, Arthur J. Gallagher): costs include interest and other non-operating items, a different scope.

depreciation_amortization._notes: Alphabet tags total D&A with a company extension that companyfacts omits, so it is mostly a gap. Last resort (ADR-030): Depreciation alone, flagged derived with a note, used only when nothing else covers the year; it understates D&A, which errs conservative for owner earnings.

capex._notes: Cash outflow, reported as a positive number. ADR-064 looked for more concepts with total-capex meaning for the 41 untagged companies and added none. Measured against PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment where a company reports both: PaymentsForCapitalImprovements median 0.38, PaymentsToAcquireOtherProductiveAssets median 0.05, PaymentsToAcquireOtherPropertyPlantAndEquipment 0.92 but 37% of years below half, PaymentsForConstructionInProcess (utilities) about 9 times: components or a different scope, so using one alone would overstate owner earnings (B4 is conservative by design: for REITs the proxy should include property acquisitions, and only the sum of acquisitions, development and improvements would, which no concept provides). PaymentsToAcquireAndDevelopRealEstate, the one combined REIT concept, was tried: it moved the label of no REIT (their other inputs are missing too) and of one software company (Workday, a campus-development line), so it was removed.

dividends_paid._notes: Cash paid on common stock; PaymentsOfDividends is the generic tag KO, JPM and DUK use. DUK switched to PaymentsOfOrdinaryDividends in 2021. DividendsCommonStockCash (ADR-012 fallback, 2026-10-12) is the last resort: the statement-of-equity line, tagged by payers whose cash-flow line is untagged (Federal Realty, Cigna); component_guard 0.5 as for the other dividend measure.

dividends_per_share._notes: CashPaid first, Declared as the per-year fallback (ADR-060). G4 asks whether a dividend was PAID. Prologis tags a small amount ($0.00 to $0.03 a year) as Declared and the real dividend ($1.76 to $4.04) as CashPaid, so Declared-first made G4 fail in 5 years in which it paid. KO reports only CashPaid. component_guard 0.5: if one of the two is below half of the other for a year it is a partial figure (Prologis' Declared $0.01 against $1.76 paid; Trane's CashPaid $0 against $1.40 declared in 2017-2018) and is skipped.
